unit_label: BRBL::MOD_C::U18: Distinguish ordinary Lok Adalat settlement from adjudication and referral

payload.title: Referral opens a settlement opportunity; it does not prove agreement
payload.core_explanation_md:
Ordinary Lok Adalat is a statutory conciliation forum organised by the described legal-services bodies. It can address suitable pending and pre-litigation disputes through the applicable referral process. Referral by a court or authority does not itself mean both parties have accepted settlement terms. The conciliators should assist agreement impartially rather than impose an independent merits decision when agreement fails.

If no compromise is reached, the pending case returns to its referring forum at the relevant stage; a pre-litigation party can pursue the proper ordinary remedy. Keep ordinary Lok Adalat separate from the distinct Permanent Lok Adalat regime. Non-compoundable offence matters are excluded; the textbook contradictory wording is not reused.

self_check.prompt_text: Does referral itself authorise an imposed ordinary Lok Adalat settlement?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Referral and actual compromise are distinct.
